title: AI could squeeze out original thinking: innovation theorist
excerpt: Innovation theorist John Nosta said AI risks squeezing out the outlier thinking behind major breakthroughs.
content_html:
An innovation theorist says AI could squeeze out the weird ideas that change the world

By Thibault Spirlet

You're currently following this author! Want to unfollow? Unsubscribe via the link in your email.

AI has become good at producing polished writing, answering questions, and generating ideas in seconds.

But John Nosta, an innovation theorist and founder of the think tank Nostalab, worries the technology could gradually crowd out the rare, original thinking that has historically driven humanity's biggest breakthroughs.

Nosta compares human thinking to a bell curve. Most people cluster around the middle, he said, while the people responsible for the biggest breakthroughs sit at the extremes, or what he called the "tails."

"What we're seeing is that large language models, particularly when they train themselves on what's called recursive data — that is, data generated by AI itself — that bell curve starts to change," Nosta told Business Insider.

"We lose the tail. It just becomes one big bump," he said. "What happens there is that it sort of blends into a sea of mediocrity."

"Einstein was a tail. Newton was a tail. Picasso was a tail," he added.

'Society depends on those outliers'

For Nosta, innovation comes from unusual people willing to think differently.

"Where's the outlier? Where's the weird idea? Where's the person who sees something nobody else sees? That's what concerns me," he said of AI.

He said recursive AI systems can gravitate toward consensus rather than originality, making it harder for unconventional thinking to emerge.

"Those strange ideas get pushed toward the middle because the computational dynamics of the AI push those strange outliers away," he said.

Nosta doesn't think AI will eliminate creativity altogether. He thinks it could make originality rarer by nudging people toward the same patterns of thinking.

"Society depends on those outliers," he said.

The evidence so far is mixed. Some research suggests relying heavily on AI can steer users toward more conventional, homogeneous ideas, while other studies have found the technology can enhance creativity when people use it to explore possibilities rather than replace their own thinking.

Chris Best, the CEO of newsletter platform Substack, has said that while AI could flood the internet with "AI slop," it could also usher in "a future where there's way more creative leverage" by giving independent creators new ways to produce original work.

Mastercard communications and marketing chief Jill Kramer said that AI can serve as "an engine" for human creativity.

She said the technology can help marketers generate deeper insights and broaden the research and preparation that fuels new ideas, allowing them to do things they "could never do before."

Use AI as a partner

Nosta said the solution isn't to abandon AI but to use it as what he calls an "iterative intelligence" partner, one that helps people explore ideas rather than replacing the thinking process itself — an idea promoted by several top AI researchers, including Vivienne Ming, chief scientist at the Possibility Institute, a metascience research group.

Ming told Business Insider in March that AI is most valuable when people use it to challenge their own thinking rather than outsource it, creating what she calls "productive friction."

"The iterative engagement is where we need to celebrate this," Nosta said.

To him, preserving originality ultimately means preserving the human habits AI cannot replicate: curiosity, struggle, and the willingness to think differently.

"The treasure is in the tail," Nosta said.

一位创新理论家表示人工智能可以挤出改变世界的奇怪想法

作者：Thibault Spirlet 您目前正在关注该作者！ 想要取消关注吗？ 通过电子邮件中的链接取消订阅。

人工智能已经擅长在几秒钟内写出优美的文章、回答问题和产生想法。

但创新理论家、智库 Nostalab 的创始人约翰·诺斯塔 (John Nosta) 担心，这项技术可能会逐渐挤出历史上推动人类最大突破的罕见原创思维。

诺斯塔将人类思维比作钟形曲线。 他说，大多数人都集中在中间，而负责最大突破的人则处于极端，或者他所说的“尾巴”。

“我们看到的是大型语言模型，特别是当它们使用所谓的递归数据（即人工智能本身生成的数据）进行自我训练时，钟形曲线开始发生变化，”诺斯塔告诉《商业内幕》。

“我们失去了尾巴。 它只是成为一个大颠簸，”他说。 “那里发生的事情是，它融入了一片平庸的海洋。”

“爱因斯坦是一条尾巴。 牛顿是一条尾巴。 毕加索是一条尾巴，”他补充道。

“社会依赖于那些异常值”

对于诺斯塔来说，创新来自于愿意以不同方式思考的不平凡的人。

“哪里有异常？ 奇怪的想法在哪里？ 看到别人看不到的东西的人在哪里？ 这就是我所关心的，”他谈到人工智能时说道。

他表示，递归人工智能系统可能会倾向于共识而不是原创性，从而使非常规思维更难出现。

“这些奇怪的想法被推向中间，因为人工智能的计算动力学将那些奇怪的异常值推开了，”他说。

诺斯塔并不认为人工智能会完全消除创造力。 他认为，通过促使人们采用相同的思维模式，可以使原创性变得更加稀有。

“社会依赖于这些异常值，”他说。

迄今为止的证据好坏参半。 一些研究表明，严重依赖人工智能可以引导用户采用更传统、同质的想法，而其他研究发现，当人们使用该技术探索可能性而不是取代自己的思维时，该技术可以增强创造力。

时事通讯平台 Substack 的首席执行官克里斯·贝斯特 (Chris Best) 表示，虽然人工智能可能会在互联网上充斥“AI slop”，但它也可以通过为独立创作者提供制作原创作品的新方法来迎来“一个拥有更多创意杠杆的未来”。

万事达卡通讯和营销主管 Jill Kramer 表示，人工智能可以充当人类创造力的“引擎”。

她表示，该技术可以帮助营销人员产生更深入的见解，并扩大激发新想法的研究和准备，使他们能够做“以前从未做过”的事情。

使用人工智能作为合作伙伴

诺斯塔表示，解决方案不是放弃人工智能，而是将其用作他所谓的“迭代智能”伙伴，帮助人们探索想法，而不是取代思维过程本身——这一想法是由几位顶尖人工智能研究人员提出的，其中包括元科学研究小组 Possibility Institute 的首席科学家 Vivienne Ming。

明三月份告诉《商业内幕》，当人们用人工智能来挑战自己的思维而不是将其外包时，人工智能才最有价值，从而产生她所说的“生产性摩擦”。

“迭代参与是我们需要庆祝的地方，”诺斯塔说。

对他来说，保留原创性最终意味着保留人工智能无法复制的人类习惯：好奇心、挣扎和以不同方式思考的意愿。

“宝藏就在尾巴上，”诺斯塔说。
